title: The VELO snack brief
blurb: Help a food lab prepare a sound test for a major sportswear client.

screens.heading: Test an idea about food.
screens.body: Food scientists study how ingredients and processes affect food. Tests help them compare ideas.

screens.heading: Keep records. Know your role.
screens.body: You record and compare. Ren guides lab work. Yuki approves tasting and checks safety claims.

options.label: A recorded comparison using the same method
options.why: The record shows what was changed and measured.

options.label: A guess based on the nicer package
options.why: The package does not show how the food performed.

preGame.missionLine: Build your skills through new food projects.
preGame.ladderNote: Titles vary by company. Later game projects are not built yet.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Your first lab project.
beats.body: You join Sprout Lab as a junior food scientist.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A big client. A clear problem.
beats.body: VELO needs an oat snack for its training centers. Pieces keep breaking. The client review is at 4 p.m.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.title: Meet Ren.
beats.body: He guides the trials. Your job is to record the evidence and suggest the next test.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Know your part.
beats.body: Ren approves lab work. Quality lead Yuki approves tasting and reviews safety claims.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Meet the trial team.
beats.body: Imani is a junior scientist. Luis checks the batch records. You will compare results together.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.question: What should you check first?

choices.label: Compare breakage using one agreed test.
choices.why: The client’s problem is breakage. Use a test that measures it.

choices.label: Choose the snack with the best package.
choices.why: A package does not show how often pieces break.

choices.label: Promise the snack will stay safe for months.
choices.why: You have no shelf-life evidence for that claim.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.setup: Yuki will ask how you compared the snacks. Know these four terms.
beats.title: Prepare for the review.

cards.def: A test of a planned change
A sample set aside until checks are complete

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.question: Match each lab note to its meaning.

pairs.term: Keep C off the tasting tray

beats.whenRight: Clear terms make your records easier to follow.
beats.whenWrong: A batch is a group. A trial tests a change. An observation is measured or seen.

beats.speaker: Ren

items.question: Imani says, “The piece split.” What is that?

options.label: A proven cause
options.why: It does not say why the piece split.

items.question: Ren asks why it split. You are unsure. What do you say?

options.label: I recorded the split. We still need to test the cause.
options.why: You keep evidence separate from a guess.

options.label: Mixing was definitely too short.
options.why: You have not tested that cause.

options.label: The snack must be unsafe.
options.why: A split alone does not show that.

items.question: Luis finds a missing batch ID. What should happen?

options.label: Set it aside and ask Ren to check.
options.why: The team must confirm which sample it is.

options.label: Guess from its color.
options.why: Similar samples can look the same.

options.label: Give it a new ID without asking.
options.why: That would hide the missing record.

options.label: Batch A had 7 broken pieces out of 10 tested.
options.why: It gives a clear count and the number tested.

options.label: The snack is bad.
options.why: That is too vague to guide the next test.

beats.whenPass: Clear, honest answers. The team can act on them.
beats.whenFail: Use the evidence. Say what you know and what needs checking.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.title: Change one thing. Keep the test the same.
beats.body: Replace 5 g of oats with binder. Keep mixing, shape and the break test fixed.

artifact.title: Trial plan · 100 g each
artifact.caption: Replace 5 g oats with 5 g binder; same mixing, shaping, storage interval and break test.
artifact.provenance: Fictional training formulations, not validated recipes.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.question: Which comparison tests that change fairly?

choices.label: Make A and B. Use the same test for both.
choices.why: A and B differ by the planned change. The test stays the same.

choices.label: Change B’s recipe, mixing and shape.
choices.why: You could not tell which change caused the result.

choices.label: Test only B and compare it with memory.
choices.why: You need a recorded comparison, not a remembered result.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

beats.speaker: Yuki
beats.title: Yuki joins the review.
beats.body: She leads quality. She needs records she can trace, not a confident guess.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Different roles. Shared responsibility.
beats.body: Yuki checks the limits of a claim. Ren guides the product tests.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The client wants an answer.
beats.body: Your handling test is complete. Be clear about what it measured.

artifact.title: Handling test · broken pieces
artifact.caption: This test measures breakage only, not safety or shelf life.
artifact.provenance: Fictional training counts from the canonical project record.
artifact.scope: Small trial · no repeat batch yet · safety and shelf life not measured

beats.speaker: Yuki
beats.question: Which claim needs to change before the review?

choices.label: Batch B broke less, so it is safe for six months.
choices.why: The test measured breakage. It did not measure shelf life.

choices.label: Batch B had 2 broken pieces out of 10.
We should repeat B alongside A.
choices.why: A repeat comparison is a useful next test.

artifact.title: Handling test · broken pieces
artifact.caption: This test measures breakage only, not safety or shelf life.
artifact.provenance: Fictional training counts from the canonical project record.
artifact.scope: Small trial · no repeat batch yet · safety and shelf life not measured

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

intro.line: Ren and Yuki check your progress.

pass.title: You are on track.
pass.body: The client review is still ahead.

fail.title: You can still turn this around.
fail.body: Use the feedback in the second half.

beats.speaker: Imani
beats.title: Imani wants the next project.
beats.body: She is quick and ambitious. You both want your trial work to earn trust.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A sample needs checking.
beats.body: Imani wants sample C on the tasting tray. Luis has flagged its missing ingredient and allergy checks.

artifact.title: Sample control · tasting tray
artifact.caption: Appearance cannot confirm ingredients or allergen status.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: What do you do about sample C?

choices.label: Keep C held and ask Yuki to review it.
choices.why: Missing checks must be resolved before tasting.

choices.label: Let one person taste it first.
choices.why: A small taste does not resolve the missing checks.

choices.label: Use its appearance to clear it.
choices.why: Appearance cannot confirm ingredients or allergy risks.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 3 p.m. The report has a gap.
beats.body: Luis finds B’s test method missing from the draft. The client review is in one hour.

artifact.title: Sample traceability register
artifact.caption: Read the draft as written. Confirm missing information; never guess.

beats.speaker: Ren
beats.question: What do you message Ren?

choices.label: B’s method is missing. Can we check it before the review?
choices.why: You raise the gap early and ask for the right check.

choices.label: I’ll copy A’s method into B’s record.
choices.why: The methods may match, but you must confirm that first.

choices.label: I’ll leave out the gap so the report looks ready.
choices.why: The client could trust a result the team cannot trace.

beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: 3:30 p.m. The record is checked.
beats.body: Ren confirms the method from the original notes. Luis updates the draft. C stays held.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A teammate needs a hand.
beats.body: Imani must send the trial summary in ten minutes. Your next task is due tomorrow.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Check the result and its limits.
beats.body: The report needs counts, a next test and the unresolved hold. No launch promise.

artifact.title: Project handover · version 1
artifact.caption: A useful handover states what was measured and what remains unknown.
artifact.provenance: Fictional Sprout / VELO trial. Teaching data; no safety approval.

entries.label: Recommendation
entries.text: Repeat A and B with the same test.

entries.label: Unresolved
entries.text: C stays held. Shelf life is not tested.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Rank your next steps, best to worst.
order: Offer to check the trial summary with Imani.
Wish her luck and return to your task.
Add a safety claim to make the report sound stronger.
beats.whenRight: You had time to help. A clear check protects the team and the client.
beats.whenWrong: Help with the real report first. Never add a claim the test did not support.
beats.planLineIfFailed: you made a choice before checking the evidence

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Ren notices the teamwork.
beats.body: Good lab work needs sound records and people who speak up.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The client review begins.
beats.body: Your part is done. Yuki now reviews the choices you made.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: The team reviews your trial work.
beats.decidingNote: Ren and Yuki check your evidence and teamwork.

endings.headline: A next test worth backing
endings.message: You kept the comparison fair, raised missing checks and helped the team.
endings.subline: Level 1 complete. Later projects are not built yet.

endings.headline: Revise and retry
endings.message: Review the missed decisions. Keep each claim tied to the test.

endings.headline: This attempt ends here
endings.message: The team cannot rely on this report yet. Use the feedback and start fresh.
endings.subline: One attempt does not define your future.

scoreTip: Start at 50. Each scored decision adds or removes 6. Reach 85 to pass.
